extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedians, stand-up performers, and comedy writers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for creating short stand-up jokes/bits that 'land', covering diagnosis of failures, pre-writing premises, structural pivoting, editing rhythm, and performance timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition failure
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience doesn't share the assumption your setup needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of 'The Three Failure Modes' — diagnose whether your joke fails because the audience lacks the shared assumption before rewriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise failure
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience saw the punch coming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the three failure modes; if the punch is predictable, rework the pivot or misdirection to restore surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust failure
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience doesn't believe YOU should be telling this joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the three failure modes. Consider performer 'standing' (credentials/relationship to topic); if trust is missing, either change the joke or the performer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a true premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Write down a complaint, opinion, or confusion you actually have; why is it true for YOU specifically?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-writing step: articulate something you genuinely believe. Also identify what a reasonable person would object to — that objection becomes the audience's assumption your joke will pivot off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the pivot word
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the single WORD in the setup that the punchline reinterprets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there's no pivot word, your joke is doing two things at once — cut. The punch should re-use the pivot word in its new sense; this single-word reinterpretation is the structural engine of the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Mumble Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the joke aloud while mumbling; if the rhythm is right, you'll know where the laughs go even without the words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An editing technique: the mumble should have shape. If the mumble has no shape, the joke has no shape — fix rhythm, pacing, or wording to create a clear rhythmic contour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-beat pause (performance timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beat 1: the setup ends, you stop talking. Beat 2: the audience processes (~1 second). Beat 3: the punchline lands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance guidance: the amateur skips beat 2; the pro waits for it. Explicitly time a short processing pause between setup and punch to let the audience form the expectation you will subvert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premise is something you genuinely believe
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise is something you genuinely believe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the 'Will This Land?' rubric — ties back to the 'choose a true premise' pre-writing advice. Authenticity of belief helps sell the setup and the pivot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup contains an assumption the AUDIENCE will share
rubrics_metrics.description: Setup contains an assumption the AUDIENCE will share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the 'Will This Land?' rubric — corresponds to avoiding recognition failure. Explicitly surface the audience assumption during pre-writing so the punch can pivot off it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch pivots on a single re-interpreted word
rubrics_metrics.description: Punch pivots on a single re-interpreted word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the 'Will This Land?' rubric — same as the pivot-word rule: the punch should reuse the pivot word in a new sense to create the gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: The mumble has shape
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the 'Will This Land?' rubric — affirms the editing Mumble Test: rhythmic shape indicates where laughs will fall and whether the joke's beats are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: There's a beat between setup and punch
rubrics_metrics.description: There's a beat between setup and punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the 'Will This Land?' rubric — performance timing requirement corresponding to the three-beat pause; allow a short processing pause so the audience forms the expectation before the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: The performer has standing to make this joke (trust)
rubrics_metrics.description: The performer has standing to make this joke (trust).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the 'Will This Land?' rubric — aligns with 'trust failure'. Ensure your relationship to the subject gives you permission to tell the joke, or revise/change the joke or persona.

rubrics_metrics.name: The total bit is shorter than what feels safe
rubrics_metrics.description: The total bit is shorter than what feels safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the 'Will This Land?' rubric — prefer concise bits; trimming excess reduces opportunities for recognition/surprise/trust failures and keeps momentum tight. Err on the side of brevity.
